## parp-tools WoW Viewer v0.4.9

.NET 10 / OpenGL 3.3 compatibility-host viewer plus expanded `wow-viewer` format and conversion tooling for WoW data from Alpha `0.5.3` through `4.0.0.11927`.

### Why this release exists

- This release is the stable public snapshot of the `v0.4.9-strict-guards` line before the active engine-modernization work on `v0.5.0-dev`.
- It packages the current MdxViewer host together with the newer conversion and inspection surfaces so people can start exercising the tooling on real staged client data.
- The MdxViewer app remains the compatibility host; the newer Alpha/LK format ownership and converter logic now live in `wow-viewer`.

### Highlights since v0.4.7.1

- Alpha `0.5.3` and `0.5.5` map handling is materially stronger. The shared `wow-viewer` Alpha WDT reader and writer now carry the hard-won structural fixes needed for real native-client compatibility, including correct `MAIN` row-major ordering, always-emitted `MCNK`/`MCRF` structure, corrected tile-header sizing, chunk contiguity, and stabilized placement ownership rules.
- `convert-lk-to-alpha` is now a serious real-data exploration tool instead of a toy path. It supports target-client asset filtering, terrain-only validation exports, local tileset bundling, local doodad-model bundling, and the current Alpha liquid and placement handling contract that was validated against staged `0.5.3` data through MdxViewer.
- `convert-alpha-to-lk` and the shared writer stack are now real enough for terrain-domain round trips and real-data tile conversion workflows. The current proof boundary is explicit: terrain-domain conversion is working and validated, but this does not claim full chunk-for-chunk preservation of every map-family payload.
- Object conversion tooling is now much broader. `wow-viewer` ships shared WMO `v14 <-> v17` conversion support and minimal `M2 -> MDX` plus `MDX -> M2` conversion paths, with focused reader-backed validation and command-line wiring for hands-on testing.
- Real-data harvesting and archive access improved substantially under the hood. `NativeMpqService`, unified extraction, richer terrain tensor-pack signals, raw-chunk preservation, and related diagnostics are now part of the toolchain that feeds later experimentation and validation work.
- The app and docs now frame the active host more clearly for Alpha-focused work. Branding moved to `WoWAlphaViewer`, and the checked-in migration and architecture notes make it clearer that `MdxViewer` is the compatibility shell while `wow-viewer` is taking over format ownership.

### Good things to try

1. Open a staged Alpha client in the packaged viewer and walk real map data instead of synthetic samples.
2. Run the Alpha/LK conversion commands on a small real map subset and inspect the output in the viewer.
3. Exercise the WMO and M2 conversion commands on representative assets and report where structural validity still falls short of runtime parity.
4. Use the newer tooling as a truth surface for real-data regression reports, especially around Alpha terrain, liquids, placements, tilesets, and bundled assets.

### Included in the archive

- `README.md` for the repo-level release snapshot.
- `MdxViewer.README.md` for viewer-specific workflow details.
- `USERGUIDE.md` for controls and tool overview.
- `CHANGES-v0.4.9.md` for this release summary.

### Validation note

- This release packages the current stable `v0.4.9-strict-guards` line and is intended for real-data exploration.
- The MdxViewer host has real targeted validation behind the Alpha conversion path, but not every recent `wow-viewer` converter and tooling slice has broad runtime parity proof yet.
